facts.title: Labelforge annotation platform accessed with stolen employee credential
facts.known: Someone logged into Labelforge's annotation platform using a stolen employee credential. Labelforge's security team spotted the access at 6:00 AM on Nov 2. Labelforge, our data-labeling vendor, notified us by email at 3:00 PM the same day.
facts.not_yet_known: What data was viewed or downloaded.

rows.why: Someone used a stolen credential to get into Labelforge's annotation platform, which holds three batches of tokenized ANB fraud-review feedback. Under 2.2 tokenized data is still Bank Data, and under 2.4(b) unauthorized access to a Subcontractor system holding Bank Data is a Security Incident even if no data access is confirmed. The 12-hour clock in 6.1 started when Labelforge found the access at 6:00 AM PT, so notice to the Cyber Fusion Center is urgent.

evidence.quote: any data derived from any of the foregoing, including model outputs, embeddings, annotations, and data that has been aggregated, de-identified, pseudonymized or tokenized
evidence.point: Tokenized feedback batches are Bank Data.

evidence.quote: unauthorized access to any system of Supplier or any Subcontractor that stores, processes or transmits Bank Data, whether or not unauthorized access to Bank Data has been confirmed
evidence.point: A login to Labelforge's platform is a Security Incident even though no data access is confirmed.

evidence.quote: "Subcontractor" means any third party, including any Supplier Affiliate, that Supplier engages to perform any part of the Services or that has access to Bank Data.
evidence.point: Labelforge is a Subcontractor.

evidence.quote: Only de-identified feedback samples that Bank submits through the Services' feedback feature, for improving Bank's own agents.
evidence.point: Labelforge is an Approved Subcontractor holding ANB feedback samples.

evidence.quote: "Discovery" means the earliest time at which Supplier or any Subcontractor knew, or by exercising reasonable diligence would have known, of a Security Incident.
evidence.point: Labelforge's discovery at 6:00 AM PT starts the clock.

evidence.quote: Supplier shall notify Bank of any Security Incident as soon as possible and in no event later than twelve (12) hours after Discovery.
evidence.point: Notice is due within 12 hours of Discovery.

evidence.quote: Where this Addendum, the Agreement, any exhibit or schedule, or applicable law specifies more than one period for the same notice, the shortest period applies.
evidence.point: The 12-hour period governs over any longer period, such as D.2's 72 hours.

rows.clock_reason: Section 2.3 defines Discovery as the earliest time Supplier or any Subcontractor knew of the incident, so Labelforge's own detection at 6:00 AM PT on Nov 2 starts the 12-hour period, not ExampleCo's 3:00 PM notice.

also_do.quote: Supplier shall give notice under Section 6.1 by telephone and by email to Bank's Cyber Fusion Center as provided in Exhibit C.
also_do.point: Call the Cyber Fusion Center now at +1 (212) 555-0147 (24x7). Phone notice is required alongside email.

also_do.quote: Supplier shall give notice under Section 6.1 by telephone and by email to Bank's Cyber Fusion Center as provided in Exhibit C.
also_do.point: Email the counsel-approved written notice to cfc-thirdparty@anb.example right after the call.

also_do.quote: Supplier's initial notice shall include all information then known about the Security Incident, including the date and time of Discovery, the systems and Subcontractors involved, and the categories of Bank Data affected or potentially affected.
also_do.point: Make sure the notice includes the Discovery time, Labelforge and its platform, the data categories and all three batches.

also_do.quote: Notice provided only to Bank's relationship manager, or through a Supplier status page or trust site, does not satisfy Section 6.1.
also_do.point: Do not treat a message to Dana Okafor or a trust-site post as notice.

also_do.quote: Supplier shall not notify any Bank customer, regulator, law enforcement agency or the media of a Security Incident involving Bank Data without Bank's prior written consent, unless required by law.
also_do.point: Do not contact Bank customers, regulators, law enforcement or media without Bank's written consent. If law requires notice, tell Bank first.

also_do.quote: Supplier shall preserve all logs, images and other forensic evidence relating to a Security Incident for at least one (1) year after containment, and shall give Bank and its designated forensic investigator access to that evidence on request.
also_do.point: Instruct Labelforge in writing to preserve all logs, images and forensic evidence, and suspend any deletion of the batches or logs.

also_do.quote: Supplier shall provide written status updates at least once every twenty-four (24) hours until the Security Incident is contained
also_do.point: Schedule written status updates to the Cyber Fusion Center at least every 24 hours from the initial notice until containment.

also_do.quote: at any time after a Security Incident on five (5) business days' written notice
also_do.point: Prepare for a possible Bank audit on 5 business days' notice, and confirm Labelforge will cooperate.

also_do.quote: shall deliver a written root-cause report within thirty (30) days after containment
also_do.point: Record the containment date and get Labelforge's root-cause input so the report can go out within 30 days of containment.

also_do.quote: Supplier shall reimburse Bank's reasonable costs of investigating and responding to a Security Incident caused by Supplier or any Subcontractor, including costs of notifying affected individuals and providing them with twenty-four (24) months of credit monitoring.
also_do.point: Track response costs and expect reimbursement claims from Bank.

also_do.quote: Supplier shall give Bank's Third-Party Risk Management office at least ninety (90) days' prior written notice, delivered as provided in Exhibit C, before adding or replacing any Subcontractor or expanding an Approved Subcontractor's scope.
also_do.point: Before replacing Labelforge or moving the work to another vendor, give 90 days' written notice to tprm-notices@anb.example, with a copy to the Bank Legal Department.

also_do.quote: Within thirty (30) days after termination of the Agreement or Bank's written request, Supplier shall return Bank Data to Bank in the format Bank reasonably requests and then securely destroy all Bank Data, including in backups, held by Supplier and its Subcontractors.
also_do.point: If Bank requests return and destruction of the Labelforge-held data, complete it within 30 days, coordinated with the 6.5 evidence hold.

recurring.summary: Supplier must give written status updates at least every 24 hours until the incident is contained.

legal_flags.quote: Only de-identified feedback samples that Bank submits through the Services' feedback feature, for improving Bank's own agents. Bank Data in identifiable form is not permitted.
legal_flags.point: The batches were tokenized, and 2.2 lists de-identified, pseudonymized and tokenized as separate categories. Legal should assess whether sending tokenized samples was within Labelforge's permitted scope (5.1, 7.2).

legal_flags.quote: Supplier shall require each Subcontractor to notify Supplier of any Security Incident within six (6) hours after the Subcontractor's Discovery.
legal_flags.point: Labelforge reported 9 hours after its discovery. Either the flow-down is missing from ExampleCo's Labelforge contract, or Labelforge breached it.

legal_flags.quote: Supplier remains fully liable to Bank for the acts and omissions of its Subcontractors.
legal_flags.point: ExampleCo bears liability to Bank for Labelforge's credential compromise and late report, including 6.6 cost reimbursement.

open_questions: What data was viewed or downloaded from the Labelforge platform, and which of batches LF-2026-0714, LF-2026-0908 and LF-2026-1020 were reachable with the stolen credential?

notice_draft.subject: Security Incident Notice under Section 6.1, Contract ANB-TPRM-2025-0418: Labelforge annotation platform
notice_draft.body:
To the Awesome National Bank Cyber Fusion Center:

ExampleCo, Inc. (Commercial Cloud) is notifying Awesome National Bank of a Security Incident under Section 6.1 of the Third-Party Information Security Addendum (Contract No. ANB-TPRM-2025-0418). We are also notifying you by telephone as Section 6.2 requires.

What happened
Someone logged into the annotation platform of Labelforge, Inc. using a stolen Labelforge employee credential. Labelforge is an Approved Subcontractor listed in Schedule 2. Unauthorized access to the platform has not been confirmed to include access to Bank Data. Because the platform holds Bank Data, we are treating this as a Security Incident under Section 2.4.

Date and time of Discovery
Labelforge's security team detected the access at 6:00 AM PT on November 2, 2026. Labelforge notified ExampleCo by email at 3:00 PM PT the same day. We do not yet know when the unauthorized access began.

Systems and Subcontractors involved
Labelforge, Inc. (human annotation of feedback samples), annotation platform.

Categories of Bank Data potentially affected
Analyst feedback on fraud-review agent outputs from the AI agent builder: agent output text, analyst ratings and analyst comments. Customer names and account numbers in this data were replaced with tokens before it was sent to Labelforge. Labelforge held three batches at the time of the incident:
- LF-2026-0714, sent July 14, 2026, 4,200 records
- LF-2026-0908, sent September 8, 2026, 3,850 records
- LF-2026-1020, sent October 20, 2026, 1,900 records
The data was sent to improve Awesome National Bank's own fraud-review agents.

What is not yet known
We do not yet know what data, if any, was viewed or downloaded, when the access began, or whether the incident has been contained.

Steps taken
[PLACEHOLDER: describe steps actually taken by ExampleCo and Labelforge, confirmed before sending]

Next steps
ExampleCo will send written status updates at least every 24 hours until the incident is contained, and a written root-cause report within 30 days after containment. [PLACEHOLDER: any further confirmed actions]

ExampleCo contact for this incident
[PLACEHOLDER: name, role, 24x7 telephone, email]

ExampleCo, Inc.

rows.why: Labelforge processes Retailer Data for XYZwire. The checkout-service logs and traces it holds count as Retailer Data even with hashed identifiers, and a stolen-credential login to its platform is at least a reasonably suspected unauthorized access. XYZwire must notify Retailer Security Operations within 24 hours of becoming aware.

evidence.quote: "Retailer Data" means all data that Retailer, its employees or its customers provide to Vendor or that Vendor collects from Retailer's systems, including telemetry, logs, traces and metrics, and all data derived from any of it.
evidence.point: Logs and traces count, hashed or not; the definition is not limited to personal data.

evidence.quote: "Data Incident" means any actual or reasonably suspected unauthorized access to, or acquisition, disclosure or loss of, Retailer Data, including while held by a Subprocessor.
evidence.point: Suspected access is enough, including at a Subprocessor.

evidence.quote: "Subprocessor" means any third party, including any Vendor Affiliate, that processes Retailer Data on Vendor's behalf.
evidence.point: Labelforge labels Retailer Data for XYZwire, so it is a Subprocessor.

evidence.quote: Vendor shall notify Retailer of a Data Incident without undue delay and no later than twenty-four (24) hours after Vendor becomes aware of it.
evidence.point: Sets the notice duty and the 24-hour limit.

evidence.quote: Vendor shall not use Retailer Data to train or improve any machine learning model, except models used only to provide the Services to Retailer.
evidence.point: The batch purpose (detectors used only for ARG) appears to fit this exception, so it is not a separate breach.

evidence.quote: This VDPA prevails over the Subscription Agreement and over any data processing terms, policies or online terms of Vendor or its Affiliates.
evidence.point: ExampleCo's standard DPA terms, such as 72-hour confirmed-breach notice, do not govern.

evidence.quote: Any acquirer's standard terms do not apply to Retailer Data unless Retailer agrees in writing.
evidence.point: ExampleCo's own terms do not reduce this duty.

rows.clock_reason: Section 6.1 runs from when Vendor (XYZwire) becomes aware, and XYZwire, whose security ExampleCo runs, learned of the incident when Labelforge told ExampleCo at 3:00 PM; Labelforge's own 6:00 AM discovery is a Subprocessor's knowledge, which the contract does not attribute to Vendor.

also_do.quote: Vendor shall send notice by email to Retailer Security Operations at secops@arg.example and by telephone to +1 (614) 555-0182. Notice to Retailer's account or procurement contacts does not satisfy Section 6.1.
also_do.point: Send notice both by email to secops@arg.example and by phone to +1 (614) 555-0182 within the 24-hour limit. Do not route it through account or procurement contacts.

also_do.quote: Vendor shall not inform Retailer's customers or any third party of a Data Incident involving Retailer Data without Retailer's prior written approval, except as required by law.
also_do.point: Do not tell Retailer's customers or any third party about the incident without Retailer's prior written approval, unless the law requires it.

also_do.quote: Vendor's notice shall describe the Data Incident, the Retailer Data involved, any Subprocessor involved, and the steps Vendor has taken.
also_do.point: Make sure the notice names Labelforge, describes batch LF-2026-0818 and states the steps taken.

also_do.quote: Vendor shall cooperate with Retailer's investigation
also_do.point: Get access logs and findings from Labelforge so XYZwire can support Retailer's investigation.

also_do.quote: Vendor shall supplement the notice as new information becomes available.
also_do.point: Send supplemental notices as Labelforge establishes what was viewed or downloaded.

also_do.quote: within ten (10) days after notice following a Data Incident
also_do.point: Prepare for a possible incident audit by Retailer within 10 days of its notice, including Labelforge's handling of the data.

also_do.quote: provide it to Retailer within fifteen (15) days after Retailer's request
also_do.point: Have the current SOC 2 Type II report ready in case Retailer asks for it.

also_do.quote: shall bear the reasonable costs of a Data Incident to the extent caused by Vendor or its Subprocessors
also_do.point: Track incident costs. XYZwire bears reasonable costs caused by Labelforge.

also_do.quote: Vendor shall request consent for a new Subprocessor in writing at least thirty (30) days before the Subprocessor begins processing Retailer Data. Retailer's silence is not consent.
also_do.point: Before moving labeling work to any replacement vendor, get Retailer's written consent at least 30 days in advance. Silence is not consent.

also_do.quote: Vendor shall store Retailer Data only in the United States or Canada.
also_do.point: Any change to where the labeling data is held, such as a new vendor or migration, must keep it in the US or Canada.

also_do.quote: Vendor shall bind each Subprocessor in writing to obligations at least as protective as this VDPA, and remains liable for each Subprocessor's acts and omissions.
also_do.point: Any renegotiated or replacement labeling contract must carry VDPA-level obligations.

recurring.summary: Vendor must obtain an annual SOC 2 Type II report covering the Services.

legal_flags.quote: Vendor shall not permit any Subprocessor other than those listed in Appendix B to process Retailer Data without Retailer's prior written consent.
legal_flags.point: Labelforge is not in Appendix B or Amendment No. 1, yet it has held ARG batches since November 2025. This may be an unapproved Subprocessor unless separate written consent exists.
If Retailer was only informed, for example through ExampleCo's Trust Center process, that is not consent under this contract.

legal_flags.quote: Any acquirer's standard terms do not apply to Retailer Data unless Retailer agrees in writing.
legal_flags.point: If Labelforge was engaged under ExampleCo's standard subprocessor process rather than this VDPA, that process does not bind Retailer.

open_questions: Has Retailer given separate written consent to Labelforge as a Subprocessor outside Appendix B?
What data in batch LF-2026-0818 was viewed or downloaded, and when did the unauthorized access begin?
Where does Labelforge store and process the data? It must be the US or Canada only (3.3).
Does XYZwire's or ExampleCo's contract with Labelforge bind it to VDPA-level obligations (5.3), including encryption (4.2) and an incident-reporting deadline short enough for the 24-hour notice?
Did Labelforge fully delete batch LF-2025-1103, including any backups or derived labels, by 2026-05-02?
Is sending data out for labeling within the Services and Retailer's written instructions (3.1)?
Which entity (XYZwire or ExampleCo) contracted with Labelforge, and who sends the notice as Vendor?
What containment steps have been taken (credential revoked, sessions killed, logs preserved) so the notice's steps-taken section can be filled in?

What happened

Labelforge's security team spotted the access at 6:00 AM PT (UTC-8) on November 2, 2026. Labelforge notified us by email at 3:00 PM PT the same day.

What is not yet known

rows.why: Both Labelforge batches were de-identified under the HIPAA Safe Harbor method and used only to improve AHS's own claims-triage feature, so under Section 2.3 they are not PHI and fall outside the BAA. The BAA's reporting duties cover only PHI and ePHI, so this incident triggers no notice to Amazing Health System, provided the de-identification holds up.

evidence.quote: Information de-identified in accordance with this Section 2.3 is not PHI and is not subject to this BAA.
evidence.point: Safe Harbor de-identified data is outside the BAA entirely.

evidence.quote: Business Associate may de-identify PHI only in accordance with the safe harbor method at 45 C.F.R. § 164.514(b)(2), and may use the de-identified information only to provide and improve the services under the Underlying Agreements.
evidence.point: Both batches used Safe Harbor and were sent to improve AHS's claims-triage agent feature, which meets both conditions.

evidence.quote: "Security Incident" has the meaning given in 45 C.F.R. § 164.304, limited to incidents involving ePHI that Business Associate or its Subcontractors create, receive, maintain or transmit for Covered Entity.
evidence.point: A Security Incident requires ePHI. Data that is not PHI cannot qualify.

evidence.quote: Business Associate shall report to Covered Entity any Breach of Unsecured PHI without unreasonable delay and in no event later than ten (10) calendar days after Discovery.
evidence.point: The Breach duty reaches only Unsecured PHI.

evidence.quote: Business Associate shall report to Covered Entity any use or disclosure of PHI not provided for by this BAA within ten (10) calendar days after becoming aware of it.
evidence.point: The impermissible-disclosure duty also reaches only PHI.

evidence.quote: Terms used but not defined in this BAA have the meanings given in the HIPAA Rules (45 C.F.R. Parts 160 and 164), including "Breach," "Discovery," "Protected Health Information" ("PHI"), "Electronic Protected Health Information" ("ePHI") and "Unsecured Protected Health Information."
evidence.point: PHI takes its HIPAA meaning, which excludes properly de-identified data.

open_questions: Confirm that the Safe Harbor de-identification of LF-2026-0602 and LF-2026-0915 was complete. This includes checking free-text reviewer feedback for residual identifiers and confirming ExampleCo had no actual knowledge that the remaining data could identify individuals (45 C.F.R. § 164.514(b)(2)(ii)). If either batch fails, it is PHI and Sections 4.1–4.3 apply.
Confirm with Labelforge and internal teams that Labelforge held no other Amazing Health System data (PHI, ePHI or limited data sets) outside these two batches.

If any PHI turns up, the clocks are already running. The Section 4.2 five-business-day Security Incident clock runs from ExampleCo's awareness (Labelforge's email of Nov 2, 3:00 PM). Discovery under Section 4.1 could be imputed from Labelforge's 6:00 AM detection if Labelforge is treated as ExampleCo's agent. Reports would go to privacy-office@ahs.example with a copy to iso@ahs.example (Section 4.4).
Retain the ExampleCo Privacy review records for both batches so the Section 2.3 determination can be shown if Amazing Health System or HHS asks.
Decide as a relationship matter whether to tell Amazing Health System voluntarily. The BAA neither requires nor prohibits a courtesy notice for non-PHI data.
Find out what data Labelforge reports was viewed or downloaded, and whether the attacker could link the de-identified feedback to other data.
